tools_registry_missing_notice: Registered tools with no files on disk: ${names}. Registering cannot reach them: remove the registry record or restore the tool files.
tools_registry_outdated_many: ${count} tools ship a version the registry does not have: ${names}. Dédalo serves each tool's metadata (label, configuration, affected models) from the registry, so press '${button}' to update it.
tools_registry_outdated_one: ${name} ships version ${disk_version}, but the registry still has ${registry_version}. Dédalo serves each tool's metadata (label, configuration, affected models) from the registry, so press '${button}' to update it.
tools_version_mismatch: The registry has ${registry_version}, this tool now ships ${disk_version}
unable_to_open_window: The browser blocked the new window. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.
update_code_build_unchanged: unchanged: the build wrote no new file
update_code_check_backup_root_outside_tr: Backup root outside the code tree
update_code_check_disk_space: Free disk space where the update stages
update_code_check_release_version_matche: Release version comes from the ref
update_code_check_runtime_data_outside_t: Runtime data outside the code tree
update_code_connection_lost: Connection lost — the update may still be running on the server. Reopen this panel to re-attach, and do not start another update.
update_code_copy_failed: Select and copy it by hand
update_code_delete_point_confirm: Delete the restore point %s? The code copy it holds is removed from disk and cannot be recovered.
update_code_delete_reason_live_rollback: This is the rollback for the code running now — the newest copy this server could boot back into. Delete an older one, or update first so a newer rollback exists.
update_code_dev_channel_note: Also offers developer builds made from the 'master' branch: the latest integrated code, not yet released. A developer build may carry the same version number as the installed one, and is then installed over it. Use them to test development work, never on a production installation.
update_code_dev_refused: To avoid accidental overwrites, the development installation does not allow updating the code.
update_code_host_updater_note_absent: Updates are run on the Docker host: choose a release under "Check available updates" to see its command. To request updates from this panel instead, install the host updater there (sudo ./deploy/dedalo-image-updater.sh install-units).
update_code_host_updater_note_stale: The host updater has not checked in for a while: requests made here would wait. Check its timer on the Docker host (systemctl status dedalo-image-updater.timer), or run the update command there.
update_code_image_build_note: Each update builds the new image on the Docker host: slower than pulling, and it needs the checkout's git remote and the package mirrors to be reachable from there.
update_code_image_command_note: Run it on the Docker host, in the stack directory (the one holding .dedalo.env). It takes a database backup, installs the image, and rolls back by itself if the new version does not come up healthy.
update_code_image_engine_back: The engine is back; reading the recorded outcome…
update_code_image_follow_timeout: This panel stopped following the update. Reopen it later to see the outcome.
update_code_image_mode_build: Built on the Docker host from its checkout
update_code_image_refused_dev_channel_no: This installation runs a release: move it onto developer images on the Docker host (run the update command there with the -dev version); after that, developer updates can be requested here.
update_code_image_refused_host_updater_n: The host updater is not running on the Docker host. Run the update command there instead.
update_code_image_refused_malformed_vers: That release has no valid version number.
update_code_image_refused_no_request: There is no pending update request.
update_code_image_refused_not_image_chan: This installation does not run from a container image: update it with the code update.
update_code_image_refused_request_claime: The host updater has already started this update: it can no longer be cancelled.
update_code_image_refused_request_pendin: An image update is already requested or running.
update_code_image_refused_version_refuse: That release is not on the upgrade path from the running version: install the releases in order.
update_code_image_request_claimed_note: The host updater is installing the update (backup, image, health check)…
update_code_image_request_gone: The request is no longer pending, and no outcome was recorded for it.
update_code_image_requested: Update requested. The host updater starts it within a minute; this panel follows it.
update_code_image_waiting_engine: The engine is being replaced on the Docker host…
update_code_lead: Downloads, verifies and installs a new code release, then restarts. The previous tree is kept as a restore point.
update_code_no_updates: There are no updates available for your version.
update_code_note_archive_installable: The installer refuses an entire archive that contains a symlink entry.
update_code_note_backup_fresh: A code update refuses without a recent backup, unless the request waives it.
update_code_note_channel_image: This install runs from a container image; a code swap would be discarded on the next recreation. Update the image instead.
update_code_note_disk_space: An update needs room for a second copy of the code tree (the release plus its dependencies) before anything is swapped. The exact requirement is measured when the update starts.
update_code_note_no_restore_points: No previous code backup on disk.
update_code_note_release_ref_current: Integrated on 'master' but not released yet: these commits reach installations only through a developer build until a new vX.Y.Z tag is cut.
update_code_note_release_tag: A published release is built from a vX.Y.Z git tag of this engine, never from a branch tip nor from a pre-release (beta) tag; until the first one exists, this code reaches installations only as developer builds. To publish, tag the release commit on the remote and fetch tags into the build checkout.
update_code_note_root_entries: A release must ship every root entry, or the swap moves the unknown ones into the backup and refuses.
update_code_note_supervisor: Without a supervisor the server would stop after the swap and not come back.
update_code_note_worktree_dirty: Uncommitted changes are NOT included: a build archives committed refs (the release tag or 'master').
update_code_ready_with_waiver: Ready to update, but only with a waiver
update_code_reload_required: Reload required: log in again to load the new code.
update_code_restore_bun_versions: This copy pins Bun %s; this server runs Bun %s. Install Bun %s to restore it.
update_code_restore_confirm_downgrade: I understand this installation will run version %s while the database stays as it is
update_code_restore_connection_lost: Connection lost — the restore may still be running on the server. Reopen this panel to re-attach, and do not start another restore.
update_code_restore_note_becomes_restore: The code running now is kept as a new restore point.
update_code_restore_note_migrations: Database changes already applied are NOT undone: restoring older code does not revert them.
update_code_restore_reason_bun_pin_misma: This copy pins a different Bun runtime than the one running. Install the pinned Bun first.
update_code_restore_reason_not_bootable: This copy is incomplete (no package.json or no node_modules) and cannot be restored.
update_code_restore_reason_unknown_versi: This copy does not declare a Dédalo version, so it cannot be restored.
update_code_restore_rolled_back: The restore was rolled back — the server is running the code it was running before.
update_code_rolled_back: The update was rolled back — the server is running the previous version.
update_code_server_gone: The server did not come back — check the logs.
update_code_tree_swap_readiness: In-place code update (not used by this installation)
update_code_unconfirmed: The server is back and running version %s. This panel was reopened after the run started, so it cannot confirm by itself whether the operation completed — compare that version with the one you expected.
update_code_waive_backup: Update without a recent database backup
update_code_waive_backup_note: The database will not be restorable if the update goes wrong. Make a backup first whenever you can; every waiver is recorded in the server log with your user.
update_code_waive_backup_now_required: The database backup went stale while this dialog was open. Make a backup, or accept the waiver below, then press Update again.
update_ontology_code_older: Your Dédalo code is older than this ontology needs (≥ %s). Update the code soon to avoid incompatibilities.
update_ontology_connect_body: The list above is built from ONTOLOGY_SERVERS in ../private/.env (one JSON array, one object per master). Add the servers you are authorized to pull from and restart the server.
update_ontology_connect_title: Connect to a remote ontology server
update_ontology_field_code_info: The ONTOLOGY_SERVER_CODE configured on THAT server. A wrong or missing code makes it answer as unreachable.
update_ontology_field_name_info: Free label, only shown in the list above.
update_ontology_field_url_info: The master’s JSON API endpoint, ending in /dedalo/core/api/v1/json/.
update_ontology_lead: Overwrites the live ontology with a snapshot from a master server. Irreversible.
update_ontology_overwrite_note: Overwrites the local ontology. Imports a snapshot from the selected master over the live ontology. Local ontology edits are lost, and this can’t be undone.
update_ontology_select_tld_alert: Select at least one ontology to update.
update_ontology_tlds_empty_master_none: the master returned no list — check its access code
update_ontology_tlds_empty_select_master: select a master, then fetch its list
update_ontology_tlds_note: The list below is yours to edit — it is remembered in this browser and is never overwritten when you pick a master.
update_ontology_tlds_origin_env: It starts from ACTIVE_ONTOLOGY_TLDS in ../private/.env — the shared TLDs this installation tracks — always unioned with the core pair ontology / ontologytype. Change it there to change the default for everyone.
update_ontology_tlds_origin_fallback: ACTIVE_ONTOLOGY_TLDS is not set in ../private/.env, so it starts from the engine’s built-in fallback (below), unioned with the core pair ontology / ontologytype. Domain TLDs (oh, ich, tch, numisdata, …) are per-installation: set the key to make your own set the default for everyone.
update_ontology_unreachable_error: Could not reach the master server.
user_section_id: User section_id or a sequence as 1,2,3
will_open_all_related_records: This will open all related data of {0} of all records in a new window without filtering. Are you sure?
